name: Guts
description: Guts is a high-stakes poker variant known for its rapidly escalating pots and simple 'in or out' decision-making. Players receive 2-3 cards and simultaneously declare whether they're 'in' (competing for the pot) or 'out' (folding). Losers must match the entire pot, causing explosive pot growth. The name refers to the bravery required to risk large sums.

history.origins: Developed in the United States as a dealer's choice poker variant. The exact origin is unknown, but it became popular in home games and casinos in the mid-20th century.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Guts emerges in American poker games.
1970s-1980s: Gains popularity in dealer's choice games.
Present: Played in home games and some casinos; known for wild pot swings.
history.cultural: Represents American gambling culture's love of high-risk, high-reward games.
history.evolution: Evolved from simple two-card poker into numerous variants with different card counts and betting structures.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 2 or 3 cards (variant-dependent). No community cards. Simultaneous in/out declaration.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best hand among players who declare 'in', or be the only player to declare 'in'.
rules.gameplay: If the pot is empty, all players pay the agreed ante. Dealer shuffles and deals two cards face down to each player. Starting left of dealer and going clockwise, each player declares in (compete for the pot) or out (drop out; no extra loss). If more than one stays in, they show hands and the best two-card hand wins the pot. All players who stayed in but did not win must each pay an amount equal to the whole pot into the next deal. If only one stays in, that player takes the pot without showing. Ties for best share the pot; if all who stayed in tie, pot may be carried or re-anted as agreed.
keyRules: Two cards each, dealt one at a time face down. Declare in or out in turn (or simultaneously by chips in fist, if agreed). Best two-card hand among those in wins: pair beats non-pair, higher pair beats lower, then highest card then second. Aces high. Losers who stayed in each match the pot. Agree ante and optional max loss per deal before play.

strategy.basic: Only go 'in' with a pair or Ace-high. The risk of matching the pot is enormous.
strategy.intermediate: Pot Odds Calculation: If the pot is $100 and you have a 50% chance to win, you're risking $100 to win $100. You need better than 50% to make it profitable.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing: In games with experienced players, going 'in' with a weak hand can sometimes scare others into going 'out', winning you the pot uncontested. But this is extremely risky.
tips: The pot can double or triple in a single round. Be cautious.
If the pot is huge, even strong hands become risky. Know when to fold.
Survivor Guts (where only the worst hand matches the pot) is less volatile.

variations.name: Simultaneous Declare
variations.description: All players declare in or out at once, e.g. on dealer's call of 1-2-3-DROP (drop cards to be out) or using chips in closed fist (chip = in). No sequential bluffing.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes declaration timing only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Single Loser, Ante on All Deals
variations.description: Only the player with the worst hand among those in matches the pot. Players ante every deal; only whoever had to match the pot is excused from ante on the next deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes who matches pot; no engine constant overrides documented.

variations.name: Kitty or Ghost
variations.description: An extra hand (ghost) is dealt and exposed at showdown. To win you must beat the ghost and other players. If ghost wins, everyone who stayed in matches the pot.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds ghost hand; overrides would need custom logic, not constants.

variations.name: Three-Card Guts
variations.description: Each player receives three cards. Hand ranking usually: three of a kind, straight flush, straight, flush, pair, nothing. Declaration and match-pot procedure same as two-card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses three cards and different hand ranks; engine overrides not yet mapped.
